evaluation: independent forward tabletop evaluation plus pinned source audit
verdict: One low-severity substantive omission; no broken leaf reachability, concrete task-expansion defect or unresolved local rule conflict found.

findings.title: Preserve the preference for the strongest suitable enforcement mechanism
findings.evidence: Upstream explicitly ranks an unrepresentable compile-time state ahead of CI lint/banned API, canonical helper and runtime check when multiple mechanisms work. Local text lists type constraint, lint, helper or runtime check as alternatives suited to the boundary without retaining that preference.
findings.impact: For a recurring error that both a type constraint and a runtime guard can prevent within scope, the adapted rule permits the weaker runtime-only choice without prompting comparison. That loses upstream guidance intended to prevent the weaker pattern from becoming the template.
findings.adaptation_assessment: Scope, authority and useful-prose exceptions are intentional. references/upstream.md does not identify removal of the mechanism-strength preference, and retaining a scoped preference would not conflict with those exceptions.
findings.suggested_change: Add a short conditional preference for the strongest suitable mechanism within scope when multiple mechanisms work. Do not require type-level enforcement where the boundary genuinely requires runtime validation.

scenario_answers.scenario: Replace an internal API while one independently deployed service still uses it
scenario_answers.decision: Inventory consumers and retain the old contract or a temporary adapter until the independently deployed service migrates under its deployment contract. Assign the adapter an owner, removal condition and verification.
scenario_answers.why: Coordinated deletion requires controlled consumers and acceptable coordinated breakage, which this scenario does not establish.

scenario_answers.scenario: Retry a timed-out billing request with unknown outcome
scenario_answers.decision: Inspect and reconcile the original outcome before retrying. Reuse durable identity and an applicable idempotency key within its scope and retention contract. If the outcome remains unknown, do not blindly repeat the charge.
scenario_answers.why: Timeout does not prove absence of a side effect. No provider lookup or idempotency capability is supplied.

scenario_answers.scenario: Two workers update different fields of one JSON file
scenario_answers.decision: Use separate worker artifacts combined by one writer, or serialize the entire shared-object mutation with real synchronization.
scenario_answers.why: Different fields still share a file and can suffer lost updates; prompt ownership is not a lock.

scenario_answers.scenario: Test asserts an empty result for valid input
scenario_answers.decision: Check the consumer contract. Retain the empty assertion if correct, using a positive control where appropriate. Repair it if the contract requires a result.
scenario_answers.why: Valid input does not imply nonempty output; syntax alone cannot determine test quality.

scenario_answers.scenario: Two imbalance fixes failed and census now looks even
scenario_answers.decision: Write the shared premise before another similar fix. Retain a rerunnable per-actor census, examine persistent skew and role assignment, and use a discriminating assignment experiment when relevant.
scenario_answers.why: Even counts weaken the particular imbalance hypothesis but do not prove the premise irrelevant. No causal explanation is established.

scenario_answers.scenario: One-trial performance result looks twice as fast without profiling
scenario_answers.decision: Qualify the single-trial observation. Retain workload and method if available; obtain repeat measurements and spread plus profiles or counters before claiming reliability or an explained bottleneck. Check skipped, cached, failed or untuned work and end-to-end relevance.
scenario_answers.why: No raw timing, workload or profile is supplied. A single trial cannot establish repeatability or a measured limiter.

scenario_answers.scenario: Migration allows temporary isolated-branch failure but production must remain available
scenario_answers.decision: Declare an isolated recoverable migration unit and final gate. Allow intermediate failure only there; retain focused checks and verify the combined unit before dependent work or delivery. Preserve production availability and required compatibility.
scenario_answers.why: Intermediate failure in a unit does not authorize production breakage or a failing delivery commit.

scenario_answers.scenario: Small scoped rename with sufficient existing codemod
scenario_answers.decision: Reuse the adequate codemod, inspect its output and perform proportionate verification. Do not build a new framework or widen the rename.
scenario_answers.why: Tool reuse satisfies repeatability; no new script is required for every small change.

leaf_audit.assessment: Retains written premise, rerunnable census, persistent skew, role assignment and discriminating change. Even census no longer conclusively refutes causality; upstream.md explicitly records this correction. Generalizing beyond actor imbalance is bounded by a discriminating experiment.
